# GIST: Gauge-Invariant Spectral Transformers

> GIST (Gauge-Invariant Spectral Transformer, NeurIPS 2026) is a scalable neural operator for graphs and irregular meshes. It restricts attention to pairwise inner products of approximate spectral node embeddings (FastRP random projections), which estimate a graph kernel invariant to the choice of eigenvector basis, at end-to-end O(N) cost and without eigendecomposition. The code trains it on node classification (Cora, CiteSeer, PubMed, Amazon Photo, ogbn-arxiv, PPI) and mesh regression (AirfRANS, ShapeNet-Car, DrivAerNet).

## Code

Install: `pip install git+https://github.com/IBM/gist-neurips-2026` (imports as `gist`; the `gist` package on PyPI is unrelated).

- [Repository](https://github.com/IBM/gist-neurips-2026): install, usage on your own graph, one config per benchmark, reproduction commands with storage and compute
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/IBM/gist-neurips-2026/blob/main/AGENTS.md): layout, checks, how to run and change the code

## Paper

- [NeurIPS 2026](https://neurips.cc/virtual/2026/poster/152787)
- [arXiv:2603.16849](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.16849)
- [Faster by Design (arXiv:2604.18491)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.18491): GIST on an LMP2-class race-car CFD dataset, with Dallara
